summary: Priority inversion causing finalization timeouts and request failures on very large token budgets
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated request timeouts and 5xx failures when sending deep priming + large max_tokens (token budgets >= 150k). Unlike typical KV-eviction stalls, failures are concentrated at the finalization phase: final chunk generation either times out (504) or the connection is closed with upstream 503. Impact: Several production pipelines at GlyphAnalytics (dedicated pool) have had daily failures during long-document summarization jobs, causing missed SLA windows and requeue storms.

Environment: prod: us-east, dedicated capacity pool 'glyph-dedicated-1', request pattern: multi-part streaming (chunk_size 4096) with max_tokens set to 120000-200000, average input context ~75k tokens.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Upload a 70k token priming document via our chunked priming API.
2. Issue a generation request with max_tokens=150000 and stream=true.
3. Observe normal token emission for ~95% of the run.
4. During finalizer step (last 5-10% of tokens) request stalls then either returns 504 or the connection resets with upstream 503.

Observed behavior: repeated finalizer-phase timeouts; stack traces in runtime logs show worker stuck waiting on finalizer queue priority and a later preemption of the streaming task. Expected behavior: finalizer completes within configured finalizer_timeout and stream remains connected for entire emission.

Initial logs (redacted):
- serving-runtime WARN [2026-03-10T18:12:43Z] finalizer: queue_wait=38.4s priority=low -> promoted=false
- scheduler ERROR [2026-03-10T18:12:57Z] worker-23: upstream 503 connection reset during finalize
- proxy INFO [2026-03-10T18:13:01Z] streaming-conn-451: client EOF after 1.3s of inactivity

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support increased finalizer concurrency on glyph-dedicated-1 (small Bump) and set finalizer_timeout to 120s; customer reports fewer failures but still sees intermittent resets on the largest budgets.
- Advised customer to split jobs into smaller max_tokens windows as a workaround.

Investigation notes (Eng):
- Hypothesis A: priority inversion between streaming emission tasks (high I/O) and finalizer tasks (CPU/serialization) allows high-priority streaming to be preempted by unrelated batch work; when finalizer wakes it finds streaming connection closed.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache flush/serialization at very large sequence lengths causes blocking I/O from storage layer while scheduler holds token-emitter slots, resulting in apparent finalizer stall.
- Collected traces show scheduler context switches around finalizer wakes and a correlation between long GC/serialization events and connection resets.
- Trace link: https://sentry.internal.redwood.ai/issue/9876 (redacted)

Next steps:
1) Run targeted repro on dedicated repro cluster with identical capacity and input sizes (owner: eng-repro team).
2) Add telemetry to finalizer queue for priority/promotions and measure time-in-queue per request.
3) Try a patch to temporarily bias finalizer tasks to higher real-time priority in the scheduler and validate if failure rate drops.
4) If confirmed, schedule a controlled rollout of priority-fix with feature flag and monitor.

Customer impact and follow-up:
- Customer is on a dedicated contract; CS has escalated to enterprise support. They require a postmortem and a timeline for a permanent fix.
- Proposed interim SLA concession: credit for failed jobs during investigation window (customer agreed to credits pending resolution).
